subject: Recap: LumenHealth expansion call — economics & action items
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Jones <samantha.jones@lumenhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 02 Mar 2028 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Recap: LumenHealth expansion call — economics & action items

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned: 

Call highlights
- Current: ~50M tokens/month (production queries) running on hosted Redwood models.
- Near-term plan: Q3 target is to scale to ~250M tokens/month with additional routes for 32k-context and reranking workloads.
- Key asks from LumenHealth: predictable $/1M token economics for budgeting, a blended rate if we mix routes/models, and an option for dedicated capacity if latency/SLAs become critical.

Preliminary unit-econ and pricing notes (ballpark numbers for discussion)
- Baseline hosted model (standard gen): $750 / 1M tokens (example committed-rate)
- Large-context / specialized route: $1,850 / 1M tokens
- Example blended run-rate for a 250M mix (60% standard, 40% large): ~$(0.6*750 + 0.4*1850) = $1,120 / 1M tokens (illustrative)

Budget range you mentioned on the call
- You indicated a target budget range closer to ~$700–$950 / 1M tokens depending on commitments and routes. We can propose a couple of structures to hit a target blended rate in that range with committed volume and routing mix.

Proposed two-track offer (next steps)
1) Committed blended: propose a committed 12-month volume (e.g., 250–300M TPM) with a blended target rate we agree on; commit tiers produce lower blended $/1M.
2) Hybrid: Dedicated capacity credit + overage pricing for burst months; good when latency-sensitive routes increase.

Action items
- I attached a quick mutual action plan (MUTUAL_ACTION_PLAN_LumenHealth.xlsx) and a short pricing sketch (redwood-blend-pricing-v1.pdf) for internal review.
- Marissa will run pricing scenarios and circulate two concrete options (tiered committed vs hybrid) by Friday EOD PT.
- Ben and I will prepare a short routing/playbook doc showing how we would map request types to model variants to keep costs efficient.
- Samantha/procurement: confirm target budget band and preferred PO/contract timeline — you mentioned procurement review the week of Mar 13?

If that matches your notes, we’ll lock timelines and send the formal proposal.

Thanks —

Diego
Diego Fernandez
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
diego.fernandez@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference

Attachments: MUTUAL_ACTION_PLAN_LumenHealth.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood-blend-pricing-v1.pdf (summary PDF)

From: Samantha Jones <samantha.jones@lumenhealth.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@lumenhealth.com
Date: Fri, 03 Mar 2028 09:06:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap: LumenHealth expansion call — economics & action items

Thanks Diego — this is exactly the kind of recap we wanted. A few clarifications from procurement and product: 

- Budget: Product leadership prefers we target ~$800 / 1M tokens blended for planning. Procurement is pushing for a max of $950 / 1M unless we can show clear efficiency measures that keep unit cost low.
- Volume assumptions: the 250M TPM assumption is realistic for Q3 if pilot goes well in May/June. We may ramp slower (150–200M) if onboarding complexity is higher than expected.
- Dedicated vs hosted: if we can guarantee p95 latency under 200ms for critical patient-facing flows, procurement will seriously consider a committed dedicated pool model — otherwise they prefer hosted with committed discounts.

Procurement asked whether you can include a line item that separates committed capacity credits vs per-token blended charges so they can plug numbers into our TCO model. Also please include support/observability add-on pricing (30-day vs 90-day metrics retention).

We can do a follow-up with your pricing team — is Friday Mar 4 at 10am PT ok to review Marissa’s scenarios? Procurement (procurement@lumenhealth.com) will join. Also we’d like a short (15m) walkthrough of routing/fallback logic for how you’d move traffic between model variants.

Appreciate it,
Samantha
Samantha Jones
Head of Product Ops | LumenHealth
Samantha.Jones@lumenhealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 03 Mar 2028 11:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: LumenHealth expansion call — economics & action items

Hi Samantha — looping in Ben and Diego on this note. Great questions — below are two structured options we can formalize ahead of Friday’s call. I attached an itemized workbook (LumenHealth_pricing_options_v2.xlsx).

Option A — Committed blended (aims for ~$900 / 1M blended)
- Commitment: 12 months, 250M tokens/month committed (3B tokens total).
- Pricing: blended committed rate: $900 / 1M tokens.
- Overage: $1,200 / 1M tokens beyond committed monthly cap.
- Includes: basic observability (30-day retention), standard support (business hours).

Option B — Hybrid dedicated-credit (aims for ~$800 blended effective with credits)
- Commitment: 12 months, 200M tokens/month committed + dedicated pool credit equivalent to 50M tokens/month for latency-sensitive flows.
- Pricing: committed blended charge $980 / 1M tokens but with a dedicated-credit adjustment that reduces effective blended spend to target ~$800/1M for expected mix.
- Overage and burst: negotiated burst pricing and priority routing.
- Includes: 90-day observability add-on priced separately at $X/month (see workbook).

Quick unit-econ example (best-effort illustration):
- If you run 250M tokens with a 60/40 split standard/large-context, Option A blended = ~$1,120/1M before commitment discount; the $900 committed blended is achieved via committed discount and routing optimizations (prefix caching, reranking batching).

Next steps
- We’ll run the workbook against three ramp scenarios (150M, 250M, 350M TPM) and show the blended $/1M and total monthly cost.
- Diego and Ben will prepare a short routing playbook and a one-slide SLA summary for the dedicated option.
- Marissa to send the formal quote PDF and the workbook by EOD Friday Mar 3 PT.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Principal Account Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0199

Thanks Marissa — that sounds good. We confirm Friday Mar 4 at 10am PT for the pricing review + routing walkthrough. Procurement will use the workbook to start a TCO model; please include a line that splits committed capacity credits from per-token charges so we can show it to finance.

Action items for Redwood before the call
- Formal quote PDF (line items separated): due by EOD Mar 3 PT.
- 15m routing demo + one-slide SLA summary during the call.
- Provide example PO/contract language for a 12-month committed term (procurement asked to see any standard dedicated-commit clauses).

Procurement copied here (procurement@lumenhealth.com) — I’ll loop Tom from finance if we need approvals. Looking forward to Friday.

Best,
Samantha
